title: A careful registry-sharing proposal to CFC International

sentences.text: At RASopathies Network, we support families affected by KRAS-related RASopathies; the atlas infers your KRAS community connection from your support for CFC syndrome, rather than an explicit gene listing.
KRAS-related RASopathies and HRAS-related Costello syndrome share evidence of overactive proteins, giving us a reason to explore collaboration.
Their symptom similarity is inferred by the atlas with confidence 0.36, below 0.5—not proof that families have identical needs.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: Your CITIZEN CFC Syndrome Registry, PATRAS and our contact registry are listed as resources for KRAS families, although all three KRAS links are inferred by the atlas.
The Clinical, Genetic, and Epidemiologic Study of Children and Adults With RASopathies explicitly names KRAS and HRAS.
Let us explore sharing registry experience before assuming that eligibility or data collection can carry over.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please confirm whether left unilambdoid synostosis, juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia and hypoplastic nasal bridge occur in Costello syndrome, and check these features separately for SHOC2- and RAF1-related disorders rather than treating missing records as absence.
We should check which individual genetic changes increase activity, impair the protein's chemical work or cause loss of function.
RAF1 evidence already distinguishes activating from activity-impaired changes.
Please also confirm registry eligibility and any necessary adaptations before offering it to Costello families.
This month, let us hold one registry-review conversation with your team to decide whether a carefully scoped CITIZEN offer to Costello families is feasible, using the checks above.
Which individual variants are activating, catalytically impaired or loss of function?
To address this, we propose linking individual ClinVar records to published measurements of protein function, rather than relying on broad variant labels.
Dear CFC International team,
I would welcome a small collaboration for our KRAS community.
Published evidence connects KRAS and Costello syndrome through overactive proteins.
Could we review whether your CITIZEN registry could be offered to Costello families?
Let us check eligibility and differences before inviting families.
Would a conversation this month suit your team?
[Your name], on behalf of RASopathies Network (RASopathiesNet USA / UK)
